questions.q: A complaint summary pilot worked on 300 exported complaints, but new complaints never reach it and investigators copy text back into the QMS by hand. Which gap is this mainly?
options: The model needs a bigger context window to read all 300 complaints at once
Pilot to production: no live link to the system of record
Too few complaints to be worth it
The demo lasted too long
questions.why: The pilot ran on a one-off export and sat outside the real workflow, so it could never become daily work.

questions.q: You want to quote the slide 4 figure that 17 percent of medtech regulatory leaders rate their data good enough for AI. What must you do?
options: Round it to 20 percent so it is easier to remember and present it as typical
Present it as your client's own number
Quote it as stated and name the source, Veeva 2025
Leave out the source to keep the slide clean
questions.why: Industry numbers may only be used as the source states them, with the source named.

questions.q: An AI tool drafts CAPA investigation summaries for the quality team. Every draft is checked and signed by an investigator. Which autonomy level is this?
options: Level 0, keep manual
Level 1, recommend only
Level 3, act and audit, since an investigator samples the drafts later
Level 2, draft and approve
questions.why: The AI drafts and a qualified person approves, which is Level 2 and the usual ceiling in GxP work.

questions.q: What does 21 CFR Part 11 mean for an AI tool that drafts records in a regulated process?
options: Each draft, edit and approval must be recorded and attributable
The model must be trained only on FDA data and certified by the FDA before any use in a quality process
AI tools are banned from quality records
Only paper signatures are allowed
questions.why: Part 11 asks for secure, time-stamped audit trails and signatures tied to a person and a meaning.

questions.q: A regulatory lead asks whether your quality team assistant is a medical device. What is the best first step?
options: Say no, AI tools are never devices
Say yes, all AI at a device maker is a device
Write the intended use together and confirm with regulatory affairs
Wait until the pilot is finished, then ask the notified body to decide for the whole company
questions.why: The intended use decides which rules apply, and regulatory affairs should confirm it early.

questions.q: Why does the regulated product model insist that people and AI agents use the same records and permissions?
options: So the AI can approve routine records faster than people and free up the quality team for harder work
So the AI never gets a back door around required approvals
So no audit trail is needed
So the QMS can be switched off
questions.why: If a person needs a qualified signature to close a record, any workflow the AI is part of needs it too.
